This paper introduces a novel feedback encoding method for user equipment in wireless systems, leveraging trainer pilots provided by base stations to decoders with limited communication capabilities. Unlike traditional methods, this innovative approach reduces pilot overhead during testing by using only one pilot, regardless of cluster count. Our feedback scheme, unlike Lloyd clustering, offers enhanced performance at no additional pilot expense in both single- and multi-user scenarios.理论研究以及模拟实验结果证实了我们 proposed 编码方法的优越性。

The recent discoveries of polarization and chiral edge currents in 1D and 2D topological surface states demonstrate strikingly consistent surface responses to external perturbations, mirroring the properties seen in bulk responses. We present a theoretical framework for this phenomenon, termed "surface currents robustness," based on the gap size at the system's boundary relative to its bulk. Analytical surface current robustness formulas are derived and validated through model Hamiltonians. The framework is then applied to examine surface responses to electrostatic imbalances in a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model and magnetization robustness on a quantum Hall bar. The phenomenon of surface current robustness offers a reliable method for characterizing the many-body physics behind topological phases.

A comprehensive examination of Brans-Dicke theory is undertaken within a spherical setup, specifically scrutinizing the behavior of photons under scenarios where a non-minimally coupled appears. Whether or not this particle can escape to a certain degree depends on the Brans-Dicke parameter, a decision that determines if it is not confined within a "phosphorus sphere." A key consequence of the Brans-Dicke theory is the expulsion of a scalar wave to the outskirts of a system, an effect that must be offset by the particle's initial conditions. A comparison is drawn with General Relativity and Einstein's scalar-tensor fields to highlight the distinctions and similarities.

We investigate the characteristics of Population III (Pop III) binary remnant mergers, considering the connections between Pop III stellar systems, their subsequent evolution, and the merger rates of Pop III binary remnants. Based on current understanding of Pop III stars, we outline the conditions that allow for Pop III binary remnant mergers and apply this framework to compute the merger rates of Pop III binary remnants. We find that the peak of the merger rate density occurs at z = 8.1 with a corresponding density of 4.54 year^-1 Gpc^-3, shifting to z = 5.1 with a density of 10.1 year^-1 Gpc^-3 when relaxing our Pop III formation model constraints. We propose a method to detect Pop III binary remnant mergers and observe that the LIGO-Virgo and LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observatories have the sensitivity to identify these events up to z = 1.4 and z = 2.2, respectively. We also develop relationships between the Pop III binary remnant merger rate and the cosmic star formation rate density and the Pop III star formation rate.

This study delves into an interdisciplinary issue combining security and resource allocation within Multi-User Multiple Input Multiple Output (MU-MIMO) systems. Specifically, it examines a scenario where multiple legitimate users compete for spectrum with an eavesdropper in order to transmit data. Two distinct optimization problems are outlined and solved to maximize secret throughputs for these users. The first variation focuses on optimizing security through varying power allocation across receivers, while the second variation explores power allocation both at transmitter and reception points. Both cases involve non-convex optimization problems that can be effectively resolved using Sequential Convex Optimization (SCO). Numerical experiments provide visual data to validate theoretical findings from Mu-MIMO systems.

Simulating text-based games large scale present significant challenges due to slow text parsing. To accelerate this process, the TextWorldExpress framework was developed, featuring a custom operating system that converts games into visually representable formats. Comparisons with existing solutions show a 14-fold throughput increase, achieving a maximum processing speed of 4,000 actions per second. Additionally, several optimizations specifically for text games have been implemented within the system. When evaluated, it demonstrates nearly identical performance to TextWorld but with enhanced compatibility, allowing for seamless integration with existing frameworks. Consequently, the framework enables the parsing of over  million real text game actions from forum discussions and Fandom pages.

FDHT-LSTM是一种基于张量分解的硬件架构，它通过傅里叶散度变换 (FDHT) 将长期记忆单元 (LMU) 的 RNN 模块转换为可高效计算的格式。该架构结合了 spatio - temporal 张量分解技术以提高硬件效率。与现有的 tensor 分解模型导向硬件相比，FDHT-LSTM 在保持高硬件效率的同时避免了额外的转换硬件需求。在多个 FDHT 特性上评估了 proposed FDHT-LSTM 架构的性能指标，并通过中值基准测试展示了其实用性。该架构在 FDHT 处理上的优越性能使其成为 AI 推理的理想硬件解决方案。该 proposed FDHT-LSTM 架构在 throughput 和 energy efficiency 方面比传统 RNN 硬件架构分别提高了 3.15 倍和 3.05 倍。

A key component in the formulation of the Weak Gravity Conjecture within anti-de Sitter space is the self-binding energy, which refers to the negative charge or charge density that a particle carries as an intrinsic property due to its mass and the cosmological constant.  In this letter, calculations of self-bound charge and density are performed using Gravitational Born-Approximation for a testly charged Reissner-Nordstr\"om black hole and the Earth-Moon system, yielding values that align with external measurements.  However, it's worth noting that the calculated values are several orders of magnitude smaller than required by the WGC, which implies that the WGC may point towards new physics at a higher scale, with possible implications for the value of the cosmological constant as well.  Conversely, combining the WGC with self-binding energy yields the condition \(\Lambda \leq \mathcal{Q}^{2}/M^{2}\), which contradicts its opposite counterpart derived from dark energy and the critical density of the universe, \(\Lambda \sim \mathcal{Q}^{2}/M^{2}\).  Given its2 approach, anti-de Sitter space might be viewed as a theoretical framework requiring a more robust version of the WGC, which could also be applicable to our universe if it too is ultimately found to be anti-de Sitter space with a very small cosmological constant and dark energy/the critical density acting as screening charges/mass.

Let $(R, \mathfrak{m})$ be a Noetherian local ring of positive characteristic $p > 0$. In this context, we examine the zero submodule of certain local cohomology modules associated with an ideal $I \subseteq \mathfrak{m}$ and determine its relevance to a specific characteristic of F-rationality for $R$. We establish that the zero submodule of these local cohomology modules is an ideal that lies within the one defining the F-rationality of $R$. This result holds true for local rings where the maximal ideal consists of test elements. In addition, in the case where $R$ possesses an excellent completion and is contained in a quotient field of a test element, we find that the zero submodule of these local cohomology modules is an ideal that is stable under the Frobenius operation, which also lies within the one defining the F-rationality of $R$.

This study develops a theoretical framework to evaluate the decision-making process of a dispatch operator when implementing a new trading model. In this system, order data is evaluated in a binary framework where complete information allows the operator to establish a link between current and future load demand. Without this insight, only statistical data on demand can be used. The decision to adopt a new design that consistently generates an all-or-none order, or to maintain the current design that gradually generates trading power, can be determined by a threshold condition. Furthermore, we investigate how changing parameters affect this threshold condition.

Given an algebraically closed field $K$ of a characteristic that is not equal to 2, we examine the typical Galois group of the absolute irreducible separable extensions formed by roots of polynomials $f(x, t) \in K[x](t)$ in an indeterminate $t$, where $x$ is subject to a degree constraint$d \geq 3$. We demonstrate that if $f(x, t)$ satisfies certain conditions related to the residues at its poles, then the Galois group of such extensions is identified as the symmetric group $S_d$. This finding is applicable to determining the probability that $f(\alpha, t)$ has no roots in $K$ for a fixed non-persistent value $\alpha \in \overline{K}$, where this probability is shown to be less than $\left(\frac{3/8 + O(d^{-1})}{\text{min}|\Res_t f(\alpha, t)|}\right)^{\deg_t f}$. As a direct consequence, we establish the polynomial analogue of the Bateman-Horn conjecture is invalid. Furthermore, we determine that if $K$ has a characteristic equal to 0 or is sufficiently large relative to $d$, then the set of values of $\alpha \in K$ for which $f(\alpha, t)$ does not have roots is infinite, and we also examine several open questions arising from this result.

Recent studies on the solar system's planets have highlighted the intricate interactions between a planet's atmosphere and its upper atmosphere. In 2019, the Saturnian polar stratosphere was unexpectedly found to exhibit a phenomenon akin to the Earth's North Polar Stratospheric Vortex (NPSV). Unlike the expected warm Saturnian polar stratosphere during summer, the pole was found to be colder than the rest of the atmosphere. Furthermore, the rate at which this cold polar region was shrinking did not match the predictions made by atmospheric models. To better understand the underlying physical processes, researchers studied the relationship between this unusual polar behavior and the planets' seasonal changes. By relying on satellite data and atmospheric dynamics models, the rate of change of infrared temperatures at different latitudes was mapped out. The results revealed that the current changes in orbit and inclination around Saturn did not adequately explain the observed polar dynamics, and thus, other external factors must be taken into consideration.

We investigate solutions to the $p$-Schrödinger equation within a bounded domain in $n$-dimensional space, specifically for values of $p$ between $1 + 1/n$ and $p_0$, where $p_0$ depends on the domain's shape and is greater than the Sobolev exponent $n/(n-2)$ for dimensions greater than two. We prove that these solutions will become unbounded in a finite time if and only if the domain no longer includes a spherical patch on its surface, as determined by a blow-up threshold $p_0$. This result isachieved through the analysis of the behavior of solution norms near points of blow-up and a method of comparing solutions to a specific function involving distances to a point of unbounded growth.

Commutative algebra typically concentrates on characteristic-one or characteristic-specific properties, yet ignoring characteristic-zero yields no significant benefits, as it lies between these extremes. This paper initiates a systematic investigation of characteristic-zero algebra, with the aim of providing valuable insights for researchers working in adjacent fields, and potentially benefiting everyone involved. We provide a summary of the subject from various perspectives, and supply numerous practical examples to illustrate the concept's applications, and the utility of parametrized polynomials in particular. Furthermore, we supply a resource directory to facilitate further exploration of the topic. Moreover, we offer an outline of polynomials' behavior under differentiation with respect to their parameters, and supply both existing and novel findings related to this behavior. With the aid of computer-assisted analysis, we discovered a set of optimized conditions under which the derivatives maintain within a specific set, and this result is offered in an format conducive to automated verification. When presented with this characteristic-zero framework as a distinct mathematical enterprise, we believe the value of polynomials as a tool for generalization and its associated benefits can be clearly seen.

This research develops a symplectic analogue of double vector bundles using the framework of symmetric double bundle morphisms. Building upon this foundation, we extend the concept to symmetric n-fold vector bundles in a similar manner that double vector bundles generalize n-fold vector bundles for n > 2. Consequently, we establish that the symplectical double vector bundle constructed from a double vector bundle is canonically isomorphic to its dual counterpart. This key result leads to the conclusion that the assignment of symplectical n-fold vector bundles is closed under opposites and duals for all n >= 2.

In this note, we establish a connection between the natural measures known as Kirillov's measure and the geometric measures on certain Lie algebra structures. Specifically, we demonstrate that for a semi-simple complex Lie algebra, the geometric measure on the adjoint structure is the square of the Kirillov's measure. This result is valid in the context of complex Lie algebras and has been known to hold for compact Lie algebras.

A novel phase-unwrapping algorithm is developed for energy-scattering-data and applicable to x-ray results, improving phase-retrieval efficiency while simultaneously yielding energy-scattering-distribution reconstructions. This approach outperforms existing methods in speed and is particularly advantageous for large datasets, such as those produced by modern x-ray machines, enabling immediate analysis on measured data without reliance on simulation. The proposed method's validity is demonstrated through theoretical proof and comparative studies using both test functions and real x-ray scattering data from macromolecules, showing its practical utility in guiding further biological research by providing accurate phase information from actual measurements.

The paper addresses the challenge of fluid flow through fractured porous media with complex, interconnected crack networks. To simplify modeling, it focuses on a specific case where large-scale blocks are separated by thin channels and derives a Dirac-$\eta$ function approach by applying the $\eta$-function method. This approach uses the $\eta$-function to describe the spatial distribution of cracks and derives modified versions of Darcy's law that account for the cumulative $\eta$-function and its derivative. The resulting $\eta$-function based model can be further generalized to model more complicated crack networks.

Decision-making can be compared to a process of choosing hypotheses based on observations, and its effectiveness relies heavily on the ability to assign values to hypotheses and evaluate alternatives. Although the concept of a utility function has been employed for decades, its precise definition remains unclear, limiting its application in both theoretical analysis and practical scenarios. To address this challenge, researchers developed a new explanation for the function's role in decision-making, and investigated its connection to assignment problems. By using mathematical modeling and graphical representations, they demonstrated that a well-defined function is necessary for efficient hypothesis selection and provides a clear guideline for training machine learning models. Additionally, the research has implications for interpreting machine learning models and uncovering the principles behind their operation, which can facilitate machine learning from feedback and explain the decisions made by these models.

To address the issue of incorporating discourse knowledge into semantic relation classification, we have developed a large dataset called DiscSense, comprising 10,000 instances that include the label for the semantic relation along with the necessary discourse markers to express this relation. Notably, existing datasets are limited in scope, focusing on specific sets of discourse markers and relations, and lacking diversity in their corpus sources. In contrast, DiscSense encompasses a wide range of discourse markers and SenseVal semantic relations drawn from various corpus sources, including Wikipedia, semEval discourse sections, and Amazon reviews. We demonstrate the applicability of DiscSense by integrating it into BERT-based models and achieving a 44% classification score without the addition of extra features, which is a significant improvement over the results obtained using BERT-based models with the inclusion of a corpus-based dictionary for discourse markers only, as well as the incorporation of discourse markers along with syntactic and lexical features.

This paper examines geometric characteristics of objective functions evaluated on a variety of matrix factorization methods. We establish that certain regularity properties, specifically restricted strong convexity and smoothness, are maintained when the objective function is factorized into its component matrices. We demonstrate these theoretical findings through a range of applications, including alternating minimization, Gauss-Newton methods, and Proximal Alternating Linearized minimization. Furthermore, we utilize these geodesic properties to develop convergence guarantees for optimization algorithms that follow non-greedy paths on the manifold of factor matrices.

A strong edge-coloring of a graph with the maximum degree $\Delta$ that is colored using $s(\E G)$ colors is such that any two vertices can be connected to at most one edge of each color. In 1990, Faudree and Gyárfás conjectured that every bipartite graph with no more than 3 edge degrees is 2-colorable for any edge. This paper disproves the conjecture by presenting an infinite family of bipartite graphs with the maximum degree 3 whose strong edge chromatic numbers are 5. Furthermore, an algorithm is introduced in this research that determines whether a specific member of this family has a 4-color strong edge coloring.

This study applies co-evolutionary algorithms to a public goods game, comparing outcomes using CGA and CGA-NE methods across varying population sizes through simulation experiments. Results reveal that CGA leads to outcomes significantly worse than those produced by CGA-NE across various population sizes, while population sizes too small or too large discourage cooperation in both methods. Notably, when analyzing expected distances from Nash Equilibrium, the social learning case displays a U-shaped distance pattern, in contrast to the monotonic distance observation of the individual learning case. Furthermore, applying the CGA method to a Prisoner's Dilemma yields outcomes aligning most closely with the Nash Equilibrium, whereas the CGA-NE method yields outcomes cooperative strategies thrive.

Consider a weighted oriented graph $\mathcal{O}(\Gamma)$ defined within a polynomial ring $K[V(\Gamma)]$. We establish sufficient conditions for the equality of its ordinary and symbolic powers of the associated edge ideal $I(\mathcal{O}(\Gamma))$. Furthermore, we derive an exact formula for the first symbolic power of $I(\mathcal{O}(\Gamma))$.

Silent data corruptions represent a significant and difficult issue in the development of robust neural networks. Silent data corruptions are particularly problematic for machine learning systems that are deployed in sensitive applications, where even minute alterations to the data processing can have significant consequences. Our research presents diverse techniques referred to as non-uniform null restriction methods, intended to uncover silent data corruptions. These methods enhance the sensitivity of tests for silent data corruptions by permitting variations in the level of freedom given to models when searching for correlations. Our proposed non-uniform models surpass traditional uniform models in their capacity to detect silent data corruptions, as shown by our experiments. Our experiments reveal that certain non-uniform models can uncover up to 50 percent more corrupted images than the conventional uniform methods. We provide the code used in our research to other researchers for reference.

Our research extends the generalization of the simple Jordanian twist within the $r$-matrix formalism to a single loop. As an interesting result, we derive a specific expression for the Jordanian twist at the one-loop level and prove that it produces cancellation of color singularities when calculating physical cross-sections in Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD). This confirmation holds true for gluons scattering processes up to one loop and for mixed states involving scalars in the adjoint representation, also within one loop or two loops depending on the context. Our findings contradict the assertion made in existing literature that the Jordanian twist is a characteristic of one-loop theory only.

This paper presents a new method for predicting names in texts from languages other than English, particularly when there is a limited amount of training data. Names in texts can be identified using supervised learning, but the performance of this approach drops significantly for languages other than high-resource ones, particularly when there is a limited amount of data to train on. Our proposed approach addresses this challenge by using a dictionary that maps words to their corresponding languages and starts giving higher importance to words that have similar contexts across different languages. Additionally, we develop a way to automatically determine how much weight to give to these similarities without the need for manual intervention. Experimental results show that our approach outperforms existing methods, particularly for languages with limited resources and for short names that are common in certain applications.

High-energy collisions across various systems (from small like $Au+Au$ and $Cu+Cu$ to large like $Cu+Cu$) offer an effective way to study the dependence of particle production on system size. This study of particle ratios as a function of transverse momentum can provide valuable information about the transition from hadron formation to quark-gluon plasma. However, recent measurements of particle ratios present conflicting trends when ordered by system size, making the creation of a standardized reference frame for these measurements crucial. This abstract outlines the available data on particle ratios in high-energy collisions of copper nuclei and identifies critical measurements that are necessary to better understand the creation of hadrons and their properties.

The impact of a city's infrastructure layout on the spread of riots has been explored in this study. By utilizing a simple mathematical model and virtual cities, we found that the connectivity patterns of streets play a crucial role in determining the speed at which riots expand a city's geographical area. Our research reveals that in two-dimensional space, the growth rate of the affected area is directly related to the complexity of the streets' arrangement. This relationship has been analyzed for both random straight segments representing streets and for real-world cities like Chicago, New York, and Munich. The findings of this study may have practical implications for urban planning and the deployment of resources during periods of civil disorder.

This research introduces a novel bracing operator for braving expressions, which is based on Brzozowski's operator from 1964 and is used to describe the results of dividing a language into segments by dividing it in a specific way. We employ this operator in a comprehensive method for determining when one expression's bracing expression is contained within another expression's bracing expression, which is braving-regular according to our definition. This bracing-based approach to checking containment is then compared with traditional methods of bracing. Furthermore, we introduce two bracing methods for checking containment that are based on Brzozowski's operator from 1964 and Thompson's bracing from 1970, which are used to compare with our bracing-based method for checking containment and find that they are equivalent in their results. We also discuss the implications of these methods in the context of bracing and provide a bracing-based way of checking that bracing is decidable.

Traditional Visual-Inertial Optimization (VIO) models extract geometric and kinetic information from images to produce numerically valid representations for accurate motion tracking. Unlike previous algorithms that perform direct measurements, Deep VIO (DVIOP) leverages learned data processing techniques, plugging into conventional IMU and image-based optimization frameworks. By plugging these frameworks in, DVIOP achieves robust sub-pixel accuracy on complex real-world data sets, demonstrating its effectiveness in complex, real-world settings. Specifically, DVIOP delivers stable direct estimation results with a median absolute error of 0.67 cm and a maximum error of 4.16 cm, outperforming other methods on the TUM and EUROLIVE datasets. Additionally, the proposed method exhibits robust performance in dynamic, real-world scenarios, surpassing other comparable methods in various benchmarks. To further validate the proposed method, we open up our datasets and results for examination, making them available for research and development.

We investigate the principles of "square-root topology" within three-dimensional space, utilizing higher-order Weyl semimetals as an illustrative case where Jaychia-Heimkeff wedges are located at the upper and lower boundaries of a slab. By introducing a periodic dimension, these semimetals give rise to an infinite number of Weyl points in three-band superlattices. Through the modification of periods along the radial direction, we demonstrate the control and manipulation of higher-order Weyl semimorphic phases, which are a result of the cyclical variation of effective mass terms. A cyclical modulation of surface states occurs at the upper and lower surfaces, which can be directly observed using scanning tunneling microscopy, and leads to the emergence of higher-order Weyl semimorphic "doughnuts" in the interior of the three-band superlattice.

This study tackles the issue of data completion in inverse problems where the objective is to reconstruct a gradient field from partial measurements over a domain. Due to the fact that the data available is only fragmentary, this problem is inherently ill-posed and requires the use of innovative numerical methods that take into consideration the specific characteristics of the incomplete data. This paper employs an advanced numerical technique using edge finite elements and examines the impact of selecting a specific type of discretization on the numerical results. A key contribution of this work is the use of highly localized edge finite elements in combination with a specialized resolution of the interpolation issue. This approach allows for the assessment of how different choices of edge finite elements influence the ability to fill in missing data and provides a potential solution to a previously unaddressed problem related to the extension of gradient fields. This solution has no spurious numerical solutions and maintains regularity within the study domain.

Knowledge amalgamation aims to integrate various salient knowledge sources into a single, comprehensive representation. This work concentrates on integrating multiple T5 models with differing capacities into a more versatile and capable one. Determining the most suitable sub-components proves pivotal in this process, particularly when training the student model. To achieve this, we develop a saliency-based approach that guides the training process by evaluating the importance of various model components, thereby facilitating the removal of redundant information and smoothing the training dynamics. Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed method results in a student model that outperforms the largest model in terms of efficiency, while maintaining performance equivalence. Moreover, applying this technique to a series of model checkpoints yields significant benefits, allowing for an efficient model that surpasses the original in both speed and performance.

We construct, for any given rational rank $\r$, an infinite number of $S_4$ quartic extensions in which certain strongly regular elliptic curves within a specific family fail to increase in rank within the resulting field extensions, and specifically, the set of such non-growing elliptic curves within the family has a rational rank of exactly $\r$ for any rank between $0$ and $3$. Notably, this is achieved without incorporating any auxiliary parameters into the equation of the elliptic curves. Moreover, it has been determined that there are infinitely many quartic extensions within which every elliptic curve fails to grow in rank for any field extension of degree $\leq \r$. These extensions can be derived from the middle cohomology of a specific quartic hypersurface containing singularities and are characterized by their image within the Galois group $S_4$. In the process, this surface is shown to be rational, its divisor class group is calculated, and the Beauville-Bartosek rank of its N\'eron-Severi group is determined to be $4$.

Quantum quenches in multicopy Fermi systems far from thermal equilibrium lead to the continuous
generation of irreversible entropy at a rate that can be inferred from two-time correlations,
offering a way to measure this quantity in future experiments. Our theoretical analysis yields
analytical results for free and interacting Fermi gases, showing that the produced entropy
matches the temperature change relative to the entropy-temperature relationship at the
final state. As a way to validate our findings in crowded conditions, we used Monte Carlo
simulations to examine the quenched multicomponent dilute gas, confirming that the matching
between the matched and actual generated entropy largely holds even when taking into
account collisions. By comparing with the exact solution of the 1D model through the
Kosterlitz-Johson renormalization group equations, we found that the generated entropy
deviates from the expected value, but the difference remains within the uncertainty of
this approach.

We present an alternative viewpoint on time dynamics in scenarios involving non-unitary evolution caused by environmental interactions, by applying a time-twirling technique to the combined system and environment state. This technique, essentially the fundamental origin of decoherence theory, reorients the analysis of a system-environment state's decomposition into components that evolve unitarily and those performing non-unitary dynamics, thereby yielding a revised interpretation of a quantity known as the distance-speed profile. This metric, used to quantify deviations from standard unitary time developments, can be seen as a byproduct of time-twirling the system and environment's Wigner-Qiskit state. We P-Z-I-S-E time dynamics' composition, consisting of intrinsic and extrinsic components, and demonstrate that, on average, the distance-speed profile results from time-twirling these P-Z-I-S-E components. This leads to a novel understanding of the time at which system states become distinguishable from the environment, known as the distinguishability time, and demonstrates its relationship to time-twirling's non-ideal aspects in a quantum system-environment's dynamics.

This study defines and characterizes regular simplexes within the unit cube $Q_n$, consisting of $n$ dimensions, focusing on those that are invariant under rotations and reflections. The research establishes the necessary condition for the existence of a nondegenerate regular simplex, requiring the number of interpolation nodes to be odd and satisfy a specific mathematical relation. The paper also provides a visualization method for these simplexes and their affine transformations, demonstrating the approach in up to ten dimensions. The described method relies on the properties of the binary Euclidean distance matrix and can be implemented computationally.

Silicon samples were prepared using the etching technique and exposed to a neutron flux of 1x10^14 n/cm^2.s for durations ranging from 2 to 18 hours.  Following this, their etched surfaces' etch depths and carrier concentrations were monitored with a resistivity meter and a scanning secondary ion mass spectrometer.  The results revealed that the carrier concentration in the etched silicon was R5x10^14 cm^-3 higher than in the BOE-etched silicon.  Furthermore, a direct correlation between neutron exposure level and carrier concentration was observed within the irradiated region.  This relationship can be expressed as the difference in carrier concentration between the etched and BOE-etched silicon samples being proportional to the neutron exposure level.  It is important to note, however, that this finding may not be universally applicable and requires validation with silicon samples from various manufacturing processes.

Interior-exterior cycling within planets and satellites could drive the atmosphere's evolution over time. To comprehend its significance, we must understand how processes within a planet's core influence the atmosphere and vice versa. On Venus, this interaction is particularly captivating given its thick atmosphere, ongoing weather patterns, and surface features possibly resulting from past atmospheric changes. We used a General Circulation Model to simulate Venus's climate for 4.5 billion years, coupled with a model of the planet's surface to account for atmospheric change driving volcanic activity. In this study, we developed a simple ice cloud model to test if our atmosphere-surface interaction might explain Venus's current thick atmosphere and why it has continued to expand. Although not uniquely solving the problem, this model shows that the atmosphere-surface interaction can account for the Venusian atmosphere's density and why its density has grown in the last few billion years.

The multivariate Hawkes process is a widely utilized model in various fields, including seismology, neuroscience, and social sciences, among others. Particularly useful, the nonlinear version of this model can capture complex interaction phenomena. However, parameter estimation for the nonlinear Hawkes process from observed data presents substantial statistical challenges due to the influence of endogeneity. This paper proposes a Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) method for obtaining consistent estimates of the regression coefficients in the nonlinear Hawkes process generation model. The GEE approach generates an initial estimate of the regression coefficients using the predicted point process, based on observed data through the generation mechanism. Given its robust nature, GEE is capable of yielding accurate parameter estimates even when the generation mechanism's model specifications are not perfectly accurate. Furthermore, this estimation method can be adapted to more intricate Hawkes process generations that include moving average or exponential components. The performance of the GEE method is verified via extensive numerical studies.

A new concept called plasma waveplate is explored as a potential alternative to traditional half-wave plates for rotating linear polarization planes in laser systems. This method leverages a plasma channel with a specific thickness that can adjust to various conditions. The minimum thickness required functions as a waveplate with a 2$\pi$ polarization rotation rate, which is influenced by the plasma density and the surrounding magnetic field strength. A thin-layer approximation was utilized to derive necessary conditions for a range of plasma densities and magnetic field strengths, which can be achieved with experimentally feasible plasma channels. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that this solution can maintain precision over substantial power ranges, enabling rapid adaptation to fluctuations in power without the need for real-time control systems. The benefits and constraints of this approach are examined in order to demonstrate its suitability for medical applications like endoscopy.

By performing a comprehensive analysis that takes into account all Standard Model and T2HHM contributions, we determined the Higgs potential in both the $\text{h}^0\text{h}^0$, $\text{H}^0\text{H}^0$ and $\text{h}^0\text{H}^0$ sectors. We also explored the impact of the $\gamma h^0 h^0$, $\gamma H^0 H^0$ and $\gamma h^0 H^0$ couplings, calculating the potential d$_{\tau}^{T2HHM}$ in various scenarios. Our studies revealed that the dominant contributions to the T2HHM potential d$_{\tau}^{T2HHM}$ arise from the $\gamma H^0 H^0$ component within the $\text{H}^0\text{H}^0$ sector, with the minimal value of $|d_{\tau}^{T2HHM}|=4.05\times 10^{-19}e\text{ cm}$ occurring under the condition of $\tan\beta=1$. This study examines error correction properties of rank metric codes in relation to their rates, revealing distinct behaviors for rates less than and greater than 1/2. For rates below 1/2, the error correction capabilities cannot be generalized, whereas for rates above 1/2, an improved version of an existing bound is proposed. As a result of the rate analysis, we prove that the Shoup-Zémor rank metric erasure decoder functions correctly for a broad class of erasure patterns, and we also establish a sufficient condition to guarantee unique decodability from the BSS bound.

In our investigation of a specific complex layer of current conformal field theory (CFT$_{2}$) embedded within three-dimensional Anti-de Sitter space (AdS$_{3}$), we examine the behavior of a set of quadratic OPE blocks comprising AdS$_{2}$ geodesic operators $\mathcal{V}[JJ]$ located along specific complex paths determined by a parameter $z$. By analyzing the expansion of these blocks in terms of real geodesic operators across the range of $z$, we observe that they either consist of either AdS$_{3}$ geodesic operators with real positions or AdS$_{2}$ geodesic operators with $z$-dependent coefficients. Notably, in the case where the parameter $z$ becomes an integer rational number, the AdS$_{2}$ expansion includes only a single term, thereby establishing an exact expression for the geodesic Witten diagram comprising a pair of external gravitons and one $\sigma$-model field with spin zero located along that specific complex path. Furthermore, this precise calculation enables us to calculate the expected value of a complex geodesic operator located along this specific path, which is equivalent to evaluating a sharp cutoff regularized holographic stress tensor three-point correlation function (three-point function of KdV charges). In 1991, Gelfand and MacPherson introduced the concept of the B_n monoidal category of combinatorial differential manifolds, establishing a foundational framework for a more intricate monoidal extension of the B_n monoidal category of smooth oriented manifolds. This intricate framework features a coherent integral, thereby creating a link to the realm of topological quantum field theories. Combining a combinatorial approach with the framework of monoidal 2-categories, this research contributes to a more intricate monoidal 2-category, denoted as B_n, extending a well-known free Lierd algebra within the context of monoidal 2-categories. By utilizing the combinatorial approach, this work utilizes the manifold B_n, providing a more accessible representation that utilizes ordered 1- and 2-cells. As a result, this research yields accessible presentations for the monoidal 2-category and its underlying monoidal category, and it can be argued that the resulting structure is isomorphic to the original B_n monoidal category.

Lobster-eye devices consist of V-shaped mirrors arranged in a grid pattern and are capable of bending X-rays into curved paths. To understand how these systems are able to form images with reduced distortion, we analyzed the image of a stationary point light source positioned close to the lobster-eye device. As the light source rotated around the axis perpendicular to the axis of the lobster-eye device, we captured multiple frames of the cross-like image it produced. By examining the angles of rotation, we were able to determine the positions of individual mirror units that make up the lobster-eye device. Using data from units where we knew the exact angles between them, we calculated the spacing between the units and found it to be consistent with the units' physical sizes. This research provides a clear comprehension of the mechanism behind lobster-eye devices, enabling the identification of units with malfunctions from the resulting images.

Utilizing a methodology inspired by L.S. Shapley's game theory approach, we re-examine several results related to regularity for solutions of fully nonlinear equations of the second order. Applying this framework to various viscosity solutions of penalized Hamilton-Jacobi equations, we recover optimal convergence rates for level set methods employed in numerical solutions to Berge-Petrosyan-Rhodes differential games. Furthermore, this framework extends beyond this application, offering a broader perspective.

To investigate this, researchers used an $N$-body simulation to analyze the accuracy of a model that considered only density fluctuations and a model that incorporated both density and velocity fluctuations. They found that a model based on density alone could not accurately predict halo masses in the matter-dominated phase but became sufficiently accurate in the $\Omega_m < 1$ phase. Moreover, they discovered that the probability of finding a halo at a specific mass is exponentially low below a certain threshold and is influenced by $\Omega_m$ and the shape of the power spectrum. In the analysis of a rotating star with non-uniformity, the use of Lagrange coordinates presents a challenge due to the difficulty in assigning properties, such as mass and angular momentum, to individual fluid elements. To address this issue, we introduce a method that enables the specification of mass and angular momentum properties using a set of auxiliary functions. This approach facilitates a straightforward derivation of governing equations in the form of closed equations. We demonstrate this methodology by applying it to the study of slowly rotating stars, yielding both an analytical and numerical solution that align with established results in the literature.

Acquiring annotated data for machine learning models can be time-consuming and costly, especially when labeling is done manually. To make training more efficient, it's important to focus on obtaining labels for messages that are already highly ranked based on their relevance, rather than throughout the entire score range. This study proposes a method called Progressive Label Filtering (PLF) for making classification models more efficient by avoiding the need to get labels for messages with low relevance scores. In this approach, messages are initially filtered without any labels, and only messages within a specific score range are selected for annotation. This results in a narrower range of labels that need to be managed. Our findings show that PLF is an effective strategy for efficiency improvements, and using two score ranges for labeling leads to better model performance compared to traditional single-range labels.

The 2017 neutron star merger detection, GW170817, marked the beginning of a new era in multi-messenger astronomy as gravitational and electromagnetic signals from the event were continuously observed for over half year. Given the merger remnant went through various stages of evolution – from the initial neutron star collision through to eventual collapse into a black hole – analyzing the fusion process offers researchers rich insights by examining the electromagnetic signal across different stages. In order to provide predictive models of neutron star merger remnant activity in the X-ray band astronomers required simulations capable of accurately modeling the dynamic interactions between matter and radiation. While early studies used general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations that neglected chemical composition effects and a widely observed feedback loop – where one-neutron stars interact with radiation to form a specific type of particle called a delta resonance, in turn affecting the surface of the black hole and driving the X-ray emission. To address this, researchers developed a general relativistic hydrodynamical radiation feedback (GRRaDiO) simulation. Furthermore, by integrating RADCAB, a code that models radiative transfer within the GRRaDiO framework, researchers produced a X-ray light curve for GW170817 that matches the observed data remarkably well.

Urban communities experienced diverse encounters and interactions during the pandemic, which may hinder their long-term adaptability to future challenges. To adapt to changing environments, urban dwellings require novel experiences, which could be limited due to prolonged confinement orders that reduced such experiences. This study employed a survey in four European cities to assess the variety of face-to-face interactions among residents and their impact on problem-solving abilities, with data analyzed using mixed-effects models. The findings reveal that urban encounters' variability has significant lasting impacts on adaptability, necessating policy initiatives that promote diverse and innovative interactions to enhance adaptability.

A recent observation of the SAO 72446 inner disc system at a distance of just 150 astronomical units reveals a striking asymmetry in the disc's structure. This unusual feature is comparable to those observed in other young stellar objects like SL 1026 and SL 150-10, which are believed to be caused by interacting small planets or more massive objects within the inner disc system. A possible explanation for the asymmetry in SAO 72446 could be the interaction with a more massive migrating object, similar to the Earth-sized planet perturbing the Saturnian star SAO 72446. However, the scale of the asymmetry is too great for this explanation to be plausible, prompting the search for more substantial migrating objects, such as brown dwarfs or stellar companions. Using radiative hydrodynamics simulations, this study demonstrates that brown dwarfs or low-mass stellar companions can produce patterns that match the observed asymmetry in the inner disc system of SAO 72444 without altering the object's position. This effect can be attributed to an asymmetric heat release during the accretion shock, which is also applicable to explaining other young stellar object systems like SL 1026 and SL 150-10, although this effect alone is unlikely to be the cause of all asymmetries in these systems.

A numerical method based on high-order spectral elements is developed to compute
free surface elevation in 2D water flow problems with surface waves. This approach
utilizes a high-order transformation of the domain combined with spectral element
method to model the variable depth domain as a rectangular one. A flow solver
employing spectral element method is constructed and matching conditions at the
moving free surface are matched to a wave envelope model for reconstructing surface
elevation. The proposed method has been tested with multiple benchmark problems and
yields an accurate and rapidly converging solution with very high order of
accuracy.

A new theorem for differential forms in infinite-dimensional spaces, termed the surface layer theorem, is presented in this research. Building on the theorem, we prove the fundamental class of the boundary of the closed unit ball in the space of test distributions is equivalent to the sphere consisting of functions with a norm equal to one. Moreover, we identify the space of spherical test distributions as isomorphic to the quotient of test distributions by the subspace conjugated duality paired with the space of distributional charges.

This article presents a layered control system for a mobile platform equipped with sonar sensors, designed to operate in static and dynamic environments. The system consists of two levels: an upper planner that maps sensor data to create environmental representations and identifies obstacles, and a lower controller that uses these representations to generate obstacle-avoidance paths. To validate the system's performance, simulation experiments were conducted in both static and dynamic settings with varying numbers of moving obstacles. The results demonstrate the platform's capacity to navigate sonar data, detect obstacles, and generate safe paths in real-time, even in complex dynamic environments. The validated system serves as a reliable foundation for a space delivery robot prototype.

This paper outlines a novel approach to assessing the validity of information, particularly in scenarios where there is limited access to information about entities and words. The authors argue that tasks such as clickbait identification and fake news detection rely heavily on contextual information and propose a innovative method called Multi-Epoch Contextual Relational Learning (MCRL). This learning strategy involves creating a task-specific representation for words and entities by fine-tuning a pre-trained BERT model. The MCRL framework consists of two stages: initially, the model learns non-contextual information using a dual-channel structure, and subsequently, it incorporates contextual information through a memory module. Evaluations conducted on the DuWeibo and JameNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, showing substantial performance enhancements compared to the baseline CRL model when dealing with limited access to entity and word information.

In the Bardeen-Brandt-Horowitz model, a charged holographic system undergoes a mean-field Higgs transition as external charge is added, but smaller curvature corrections indicate that the transition becomes less second-order as charge decreases. Notably, the system's entropy increases due to the charge's contribution and the transition shifts to a hysteretical behavior, indicating a sudden change in the vacuum state. When the charge is sufficiently large, the average charge and scalar field exhibit infinite responses to small changes in chemical potential, and the vacuum states can be connected through a closed loop in the space of order parameters and external conditions. The model also allows for an interpretation of the transition in terms of a charge transfer between the vacuum states, and it can be extended to include a charged, non-Abelian vector.

This study introduces a novel approach to $L_1$-PCA for binary data through two blocks, circumventing non-convex optimization challenges. Building on this formulation, we propose a coordinate descent algorithm that alternates between updating the projection direction and refining the optimal threshold. We evaluate the method's effectiveness using synthetic and real-world image corruption scenarios, comparing its performance to other approaches.

Semantics labeling often suffers from inconsistencies in the annotations made, resulting in inconsistent labels that do not accurately represent their intended meanings. This issue invalidates numerous data points and hinders the effectiveness of machine learning models trained on such labels. To address this challenge, a new approach is proposed leveraging paraphrasing to verify the consistency of semantic labels. This approach manual-ly creates a paraphrase task where the agreement between the original label and its annotated paraphrase should be high. This proposal is validated on two datasets, showing a significant improvement in label consistency as evidenced by a rise in Jaccard similarity from 0.52 to 0.73. Moreover, integrating a consistency filter into a supervised model, such as SVADE, has been shown to enhance performance on downstream classification tasks.

Our HiTMap representation is inspired by nature's strategy for handling wayfinding and orientation. This approach combines a global metric map within a polar coordinate framework with a set of distinct representations that correspond to different worldly contexts. HiTMap enables a robot to navigate in different contexts using a single set of translation-invariant navigation skills. By utilizing contextual features, the robot can generate suitable head-movement strategies to build or update HiTMap representations that mirror its perspective of each context. When in a novel setting, the robot can identify its position relative to the existing map, create a new representation, and navigate without prior knowledge using translation-invariant skills. Furthermore, when presented with a goal location, the robot can derive multiple potential paths that may involve transitioning between different contexts.

Using a two-pulse lattice structure, we created an atomic interferometer with a local magnetic field that is $10^{-15}$ Gauss and $20$ times more sensitive than previous records. By modifying the local magnetic field between atoms and applying a $\pi$-phase shift to one of the optical lattices, we simulated a gravity-free Newtonian gravity well between atoms. This setup was demonstrated with $4000$ Rubidium-$87$ atoms and a phase shift of approximately $0.4$ radians in just $225$ milliseconds. Sensitivity to phase changes as small as 0.04 radians leads to equivalently sensitive detection of time delays, local magnetic fields, and mass variations, opening up possibilities for various applications including molecular creation and dark matter research.

We investigate the problem of recovering discrete mixtures of Gaussians that are not necessarily identifiable, particularly in mixtures where component probabilities are unknown. Unknown Dirichlet processes are applied to the mixture densities with the goal of easily determining the admixture weights. Our findings reveal that using DP priors on densities directly does not favor any particular Gaussian component, thereby hindering the ability to identify meaningful components, regardless of how large the sample size becomes. Consequently, this approach results in an inability to recover the true model and leads to a retrieval of components that are difficult to interpret. Contrary to our expectations, our simulations show that DP prior placement on component probabilities fails to result in correlations between the estimated and true weights. Contrary to alternative modeling approaches that are commonly used, placing DP priors directly on densities does not yield a robust method for retrieving admixture weights. Our findings have broad implications for applications that are used to analyze genomic data, psychological experiments, and astronomical observations.

GPU simulation engines depend heavily on efficient memory allocation, yet the allocation methods embedded in programming languages are geared towards general usage and don't account for the specific performance needs of simulation engines. Moreover, GPU memory allocators are difficult to create, given the complexity of GPU memory management. We developed DynaSOAr, a flexible memory allocation system specifically designed for real-time simulation applications that utilizes free memory segments, enabling garbage collection and allowing previously freed memory segments to be reused, thereby bypassing the need to reallocate them. DynaSOAr provides a garbage collection mechanism, which permits deleted memory segments to be reclaimed, and previously freed memory segments to be reused, thereby avoiding the need to reallocate them. Our evaluation of DynaSOAr demonstrates a 14% reduction in memory allocation time, translates to $40 per second savings, when compared to the cuMem GPU memory allocator, while also offering greater flexibility in managing memory.

The interaction between magnetic adatoms and dimers and the surface of superconducting lead can induce a novel state around them, as investigated through theoretical calculations using the functional renormalization group method. By examining various magnetism strengths and configurations, it was found that spin-orbit coupling significantly influences the positions of states induced by magnetic adatoms, ultimately causing them to disappear at a critical strength. Additionally, magnetic dimers induce a state that resembles that of dimensionally dependent double-occupancy and exceed a critical strength, beyond which they lose ability to induce a state. Furthermore, the induced state exhibits superconducting properties and exhibits orbital selectivity, manifesting only on specific crystal planes. Lastly, by manipulating the arrangement of magnetic adatoms, we demonstrated the possibility of generating a superconducting state with a current pattern that is robust against weak external fields, which can be utilized to erase the state.

A comprehensive study of a complex six-star system, labeled "Tohomi", has been undertaken by astronomers using various data sources including the WISE, 2MASS, Gaia, TESS, and multiple ground-based telescopes. Tohomi is an unusual quadruple system consisting of four red dwarf stars, Tohomi A, B, C, and D, that are separated by vast distances. Tohomi AB is a binary system where the stars Tohomi A and B are closely orbiting each other. Researchers have also identified three planets, labeled "Tohomi Ab b", "Tohomi Ab c", and "Tohomi Ac 1", which are thought to be mini-Neptunes residing within the system's habitable zone. A detailed examination of the Tohomi system's structure and the methods used to analyze its components and planets has been presented.

The electronic structure of carbon and nitrogen defects within TiO2 has been investigated using DFT calculations across four possible defect locations - substitutional and interstitial forms for each defect type. The results show that both C and N prefer substitutional positions replacing Oxygen atoms, with formation energies of 5.25 eV and 4.75 eV respectively, compared to higher values of 7.50 eV and 9.50 eV for Carbon and Nitrogen in interstitial positions. Each defect type gives rise to a distinct set of localized states within the semiconductor's band gap, with substitutional position defects contributing two state types - $s$-like near the conduction band minimum and $p$-like states closer to the valence band maximum, while interstitial defects contribute only an $s$-like state type near the conduction band minimum. The research has important implications for astrophysical observations of these defects and carbon/nitrogen doping in TiO2 material.

Top-quark decays into other flavor is a strictly prohibited process according to the Standard Model at a very small level, and to do so would leave its signature without a $b$-tagged jet.  We developed an approach to search for flavor changing neutral current decays of the top quark to the bottom quark via both charged and neutral Higgs boson emission in the process $t\rightarrow b(X)$ using data from the $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV Large Hadron Collider containing 39.6 fb of top-quark production.  We focused on two distinct process outcomes, one with an identified $b$-tagged jet and another without, and used matrix element methods to analyze them.  This approach enabled us to set branching ratio limits of $\mathcal{B}(t\rightarrow b W^{-}\hho^{0})<0.62\%$ and $\mathcal{B}(t\rightarrow b\hho^{\prime 0})<1.0\%$ for the charged and neutral Higgs boson decays at the 95% confidence level in the mass range up to 664 GeV, and also established limits for the direct decay $t\rightarrow b H$ of 0.69% and 1.2% for the Standard Model Higgs boson and Next-to-Lightest Higgs boson at the 95% confidence level

Recent measurements indicate that the positron fraction in high-energy particles, specifically above 10 GeV/c, is significantly higher than expected from the standard model of particle physics. To explain this observation and others, a hypothetical process involving positron production from dark matter annihilation or interactions has been proposed. To enhance the effectiveness of a planned 50 kEeV electron-positron collider in detecting this process or certain relationships within the properties of dark matter, the positron beam would need to have an energy greater than 10 GeV/c, corresponding to a polarization degree exceeding 10%. We have investigated the feasibility of achieving such a high level of polarization in positrons, which could lead to a better understanding of the composition of the universe through the study of dark matter.

To build upon prior work by Shalev, we expanded the scope of polynomial diameter groups to an infinite class of virtually free groups, lacking both the properties of having finite-diameter conjugacy classes or containing infinite nilpotent subgroups, and specifically to groups with higher Frobenius-periot invariants.

A novel temperature sensor proposal is presented, featuring a full-wave rectifier made from a Schottky barrier sensor that converts any input signal, AC or DC, into direct current power for self-biasing. Unlike previous work, the proposal achieves higher resolution and smaller inaccuracy, reaching 0.48°C and 1.71°C, respectively, at a self-generating temperature, offering improved specifications compared to the proposed temperature sensor.
